source_meta._title: Decorators are independent of world seed

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w42a, the latest affected snapshot explicitly confirmed in the supplied report. Do not run the primary reproduction in 21w43a, which is listed as the fix version.
stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 21w42a in single-player, using two newly generated Creative-mode worlds with identical world-generation settings and the exact seed -8718622960759467126. No custom datapacks, mods, or pre-generated world files should be used.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Java Edition snapshot 21w42a. Snapshot versions must be enabled in the launcher's installation/version settings if 21w42a is not selectable.
Use a clean, unmodified 21w42a client. Using no custom world-generation datapacks is a practical control to ensure that both worlds use the snapshot's built-in generator.
Prepare to retain two separate worlds named MC-238073-A and MC-238073-B; do not delete, recreate, optimize, or convert World A after recording its reference location.
Use the exact signed decimal seed -8718622960759467126 in both worlds.
Use identical world-generation options in both worlds. Only the world names should differ.
Creative mode and commands are enabled as practical execution aids for flying to a clear viewpoint and returning to its exact coordinates; they are not stated as requirements by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation that runs Java Edition snapshot 21w42a.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation displays version 21w42a.

steps.action: Launch the selected installation and wait for the Minecraft main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as 21w42a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is visible.

steps.action: Begin creating the first fresh comparison world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the first world's name so it can be distinguished from the second world.
steps.success_cue: The World Name field contains MC-238073-A.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. If the mode selector currently shows another mode, activate it until Creative is displayed.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Ensure commands are allowed in World A. If necessary, set Allow Cheats to ON.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation settings containing the seed field.
steps.success_cue: The Seed for the World Generator field and world-generation options are visible.

steps.action: Enter the report's exact seed into the seed field, including the leading minus sign and with no spaces.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Leave the generator on the normal built-in configuration: World Type set to Default, Generate Structures enabled, Bonus Chest disabled, and no custom world-generation datapack selected. Record these settings so the same values can be used for World B.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Default; Generate Structures: ON; Bonus Chest: OFF; no custom datapack
steps.success_cue: World A is configured with the exact seed and the recorded default generation settings.

steps.action: Create World A.
steps.success_cue: The world-generation loading screen appears.

steps.action: Wait until World A opens, nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in World A and the surrounding spawn-area chunks are visibly rendered.

steps.action: Confirm the loaded world's seed. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the world seed as -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Choose a reference view in the generated area near spawn where naturally generated decorative features are clearly visible. Prefer an outdoor view containing several generated features rather than a close-up of a single block. To obtain a clear overview in Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying, use Space to rise, Left Shift to descend, and W/A/S/D to position the player. Remain near the already loaded spawn area rather than exploring randomly for a distant site.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; then use Space, Left Shift, and W/A/S/D
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary at a clear, unobstructed reference viewpoint overlooking generated terrain near spawn.

steps.action: Open the debug overlay with F3. Record the full player position from the XYZ line, including decimals, and the horizontal and vertical viewing angles shown by the Facing line. Label the recorded values X_A, Y_A, Z_A, YAW_A, and PITCH_A.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible and the exact XYZ position plus yaw and pitch have been recorded for later reuse.

steps.action: While remaining motionless at the reference viewpoint with the debug overlay visible, take a reference screenshot using the screenshot control.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft confirms that a screenshot was saved; the image records World A's reference view and coordinate information.

steps.action: Close the debug overlay without moving the player, then take a second clean reference screenshot of the same view.
steps.success_cue: A second screenshot is saved from the same position and orientation without the debug overlay covering the terrain.

steps.action: Open the pause menu and leave World A without deleting it.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and World A remains saved.

steps.action: Return to the single-player world list and begin creating a second fresh world. Do not open or recreate World A.
steps.success_cue: A new Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the second world's name.
steps.success_cue: The World Name field contains MC-238073-B and does not duplicate World A's name.

steps.action: Set World B to Creative mode and enable commands, matching World A's execution settings.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: World B is configured for Creative mode with commands allowed.

steps.action: Open More World Options and enter the same exact signed seed used for World A.
steps.success_cue: World B's seed field contains exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Match every recorded world-generation setting from World A: use the built-in Default world type, keep Generate Structures enabled, keep Bonus Chest disabled, and do not add a custom world-generation datapack.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Default; Generate Structures: ON; Bonus Chest: OFF; no custom datapack
steps.success_cue: World B has the same seed and world-generation settings as World A; only the world name differs.

steps.action: Create World B. This is the trigger action that starts an independent generation of a second world instance using the same seed.
steps.success_cue: The generation screen appears and then World B begins loading.

steps.action: Wait until World B opens, nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in World B and the surrounding spawn-area chunks are visibly rendered.

steps.action: Confirm that World B has the intended seed. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the world seed as -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Return to World A's exact recorded reference position and viewing direction. Press T and execute a teleport command using the five recorded values from step 15 in the order X, Y, Z, yaw, pitch. Keep the leading slash. For example, replace each angle-bracket placeholder rather than typing the placeholder text literally.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the player is stationary at World A's recorded XYZ position with the same yaw and pitch in World B.

steps.action: Do not move after teleporting. Wait until all terrain visible from the reference viewpoint has rendered and command or movement input responds without chunk-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: The reference area in World B is fully visible, no nearby chunk faces are missing, and the game is responsive.

steps.action: Press F3 and verify that the displayed XYZ position and Facing angles match the values recorded from World A. If they do not match because a value was entered incorrectly, repeat the teleport command from step 27 with the recorded values.
steps.success_cue: World B is displaying the same XYZ position, yaw, and pitch used for World A's reference screenshots.

steps.action: Close the debug overlay without moving or rotating the player, leaving the clean World B reference view on screen for the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is closed, the player remains stationary, World B's reference chunks are loaded, and World A's reference screenshots remain available.

stor.handoff_condition: World B has just been independently generated in snapshot 21w42a with seed -8718622960759467126 and the same world-generation settings as World A. The player is stationary at the exact XYZ position and viewing angles recorded in World A, the visible chunks are fully loaded, and both World A reference screenshots are available. Hand off now for comparison of the two generated instances.
uncertainties: The report supplies a seed but no exact coordinates, biome, structure, cave, or named decorator to inspect. The plan therefore records a repeatable reference viewpoint near World A's spawn and returns to that exact viewpoint in World B.

The report broadly states that decorators are inconsistent and its attachments are not included as viewable image content in the supplied text. Consequently, no specific tree, plant, ore, dripstone, lush-cave feature, or other decorator is designated as the sole target.
Creative mode, commands, an elevated viewpoint, screenshots, and the teleport command are practical execution aids rather than report-stated reproduction requirements.

The report lists multiple affected versions. Snapshot 21w42a is recommended because it is the latest listed affected version and a comment explicitly confirms it there; behavior in other listed versions may involve different sets of underground or above-ground decorators.

If the initially selected spawn-area view contains too few clearly visible generated features for a meaningful comparison, the executor may choose another nearby feature-rich viewpoint in World A, but must record and reuse that exact position and orientation in World B. The report does not provide a deterministic coordinate for this fallback.
